subject: RE: ACME SIG request - KMS/HSM controls + rotation artifacts
messages:
From: James Dalton <james.dalton@acme.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: acme-security@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: KMS/HSM evidence for SIG - initial ask

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SIG review we need canonical artifacts demonstrating Redwood's encryption and key management posture. Specifically: at-rest encryption architecture, transport encryption, KMS/HSM usage, key hierarchy, and key rotation proof (audit logs or CSV of rotation events).

Can you provide the following by next Wednesday (10/27) if possible?
- High-level diagram of where keys are stored (HSM vs cloud KMS) and which keys are customer-managed vs service-managed
- A sample rotation log CSV or export with timestamps and operator IDs (sanitized if needed)
- Any HSM attestation / vendor doc you can share

If some of this requires an NDA/update, say so and we can schedule a quick call.

Thanks,
James
ACME Security

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: James Dalton <james.dalton@acme.com>, acme-security@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-25T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM evidence for SIG - plan and owners

Marissa / Monica —

Got this from ACME. I'll own the response but want to pull the authoritative artifacts from ops. Proposed plan:
1) Marissa to export rotation audit (redact sensitive operator identifiers where required)
2) Monica to assemble the at-rest/in-transit diagram and HSM vendor attestation
3) I will package an executive summary and timeline for ACME and upload to our shared Drive.

Target: send a consolidated package by 2026-10-27 EOD. If any item needs more time, flag here.

Karthik
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: crypto-ops-summary.pdf (summary, 2 pages)]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: James Dalton <james.dalton@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T08:40:00Z
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM evidence for SIG - rotation export

Karthik —

I exported a rotation audit CSV from our logging cluster. It contains: key_id, previous_key_id (when rotated), rotation_time (UTC), rotation_initiator, rotation_type (auto/manual), and change_hash. Per policy we need to redact full operator email addresses for external sharing; I replaced them with operator IDs (OP-###). Sample rows included.

I uploaded the archive to the shared folder and added a README about redactions. Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/crypto-evidence/ACME-2026 (shared with acme-security).

Attachments in package: rotation-audit-202610.zip (CSV + README)

Notes:
- Rotations are automated monthly for service keys; customer-managed keys are on HSM (YubiHSM cluster) and rotated on-demand per request.
- We include a chain-of-trust hash that maps KMS envelope keys to HSM-wrapped key versions.

Marissa
Senior Ops Engineer

From: James Dalton <james.dalton@acme.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: acme-security@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-27T15:09:00Z
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM evidence for SIG - clarifying HSM and CMK questions

Thanks — quick clarification:
- For keys marked as "customer-managed", are they located in customer-controlled HSMs or in our HSM-backed KMS (Redwood-managed hardware)?
- For the rotation export, can you provide a sample that demonstrates a rotation event where a key was rotated and the previous version remained available for decryption for a retention window? ACME's control requires proof that old versions remain usable for X days post-rotation.

If it helps, we can accept a sanitized example with fake plaintext test vectors to demonstrate decryption across versions.

Best,
James

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: James Dalton <james.dalton@acme.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T16:48:00Z
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM evidence for SIG - final package and answers

James —

Appreciate the patience. Final package uploaded to the Drive link and I attached the summary here. Highlights:
- Customer-managed keys: Redwood supports both models. By default, service encryption keys are Redwood-managed in our cloud KMS with HSM wrapping. For customers with Private deployments or BYOK requirements, keys can be provisioned into the customer's HSM/KMS (we support PKCS#11 and AWS CloudHSM integration).
- Rotation proof: rotation-audit-202610.zip includes a sanitized rotation event showing pre- and post- key versions. We included a small encrypted test blob and the decryption steps demonstrating old-key access during the configured retention window.
- HSM attestations: hsm-attestation-2025.pdf (vendor-signed) included.

Attachments: crypto-ops-summary.pdf, rotation-audit-202610.zip, hsm-attestation-2025.pdf

If ACME needs a remote walkthrough of the artifacts (30 minutes), I'm available this week. Happy to redact anything further.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rotation-audit-202610.zip (contains rotation.csv + example payloads)]
